headline: Fire & Public Safety Commission

meeting.summary: The commission adopted the fire chief's 2026 evaluation and heard that Maui has had 14 drownings this year, all at unguarded beaches.
meeting.recap: The Fire and Public Safety Commission met on Thursday, August 20, 2026.[[0:00:34]] The fire chief said the Kula fire station truck bay project went out to bid.[[0:06:25]] The fire chief said the Haʻikū fire station still needs final approval from the County Council.[[0:09:58]] A fire official said the department inspects schools every year and sends its reports to the state fire marshal.[[0:15:28]] A fire official said new research advises putting out most of a car fire and letting the battery burn.[[0:32:25]] Plan reviewers finished 67 reviews in July, below the expected 120, because staff were on leave or in training.[[0:42:34]] The ocean safety chief said Maui has had 14 drownings this year, all at unguarded beaches.[[0:55:13]] During the recent hurricane, ocean safety added roving patrols in each district to reach beaches without lifeguards.[[0:57:22]] The junior lifeguard program served about 450 young people this year, up from 300 in 2025.[[1:06:59]] Up to 600 young people applied, but 450 was what the program could take.[[1:21:35]] The commission unanimously adopted the fire chief's fiscal year 2026 evaluation as drafted, to be sent to the mayor and County Council.[[1:24:25]] The evaluation will appear in next month's meeting packet.[[1:25:28]]
decided: Commissioners approved the minutes from an earlier meeting unanimously.
The commission adopted the fire chief's fiscal year 2026 evaluation as drafted, to be sent in writing to the mayor and County Council.
The meeting was adjourned after a motion and a second; no vote was heard.
meeting.next: The chair will give commissioners an update in the next meeting packet about handouts from the last meeting, and add it to the agenda if needed. An ocean safety captain said drownings at unguarded beaches could probably be added to the junior lifeguard lessons.

moments.q: Question about failing school fire alarms
